speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: asked the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (a) whether the Ministry has done studies on the annual mortality associated with air pollution from human activities in Singapore; (b) if so, what is the number of annual deaths in the last five years; (c) whether the Government has an estimate on the annual monetary cost to public health and social care services associated with air pollution; and (d) if so, what is the annual cost in the last five years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Nonetheless, it is clear that reducing emissions of air pollutants benefit Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Would the Government consider developing a particular yardstick based on the methodological best practices out there, in order to derive an estimate for what is the health impact, the mortality impact of air pollution?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: My second supplementary question is what policy levers are available to the Government and what policy levers does it use to induce facilities that have made air pollution to scale back and reduce that air pollution?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: And this is important given the effects on human health which can be particularly bad for industrial pollutants.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Thirdly, what is the progress of the Government towards achieving the WHO guideline for PM2.5 pollution, in the air, which I believe the Government has stated as a goal?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: And lastly, when does the Government estimate we would be able to hit this WHO-preferred guideline for PM2.5 air pollution?

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In fact, it also varies according to the context.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Indeed, for a parameter, for instance, value of statistical life that is used to estimate health costs in terms of mortality, there is quite a bit of debate on this itself and in fact misunderstanding, even among the academics.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Given this, as well as the fact that such studies are multidisciplinary, so you would need experts in epidemiology, economics and so on, and you will spend many years.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: These studies are therefore specific to each different context.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Hence, we continue to look at these studies and consider the findings.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: At the end of the day, if there are some methodologies which we think would be useful, we could consider that.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: But at the current moment, we think that what is important is the fact that there is global scientific consensus, as articulated by WHO, that there is significant impact of air pollution on healthcare and health itself, and the costs.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Therefore, we undertake very robust measures and policies to safeguard our air quality.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: For domestic sources of air pollution, the key sources will be industries as well as vehicles.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: And we have been tightening industrial emission standards as well as for vehicles.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: That will help to improve air quality, in particular, particulate matter.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, we will continue to tighten measures and regulations as much as we can.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: One thing we also need to understand is that for a small island city-state like Singapore, our sources of pollution are not just domestic – which is, generally, something that we can better control – but also transboundary.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In any measure that we implement, we also have to consider that.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: But as I have said, we are working on looking at how we can continue to improve.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As we implement and encourage the adoption of, say, cleaner vehicles, that will also help us with the index for PM2.5.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As for the Member's fourth supplementary question on WHO, I have answered that, too.
